42 nomad visas in the registry. The lowest threshold is not worth taking at face value

The private registry WhereNext, as of September 23, 2026, holds 42 programs for remote workers. Additionally, in the same database, there are 24 pension routes, 28 investment routes, and a total of 273 paths in 95 countries. This is not a law or a consular list. It is a summary, and the platform itself states that the thresholds fluctuate and need to be verified before applying.

In its ranking, the lowest declared income is from Albania. Unique Permit for digital mobile workers, article 68 of law 79/2021: around $4,845 per year, 12 months with extensions, duration around 84 days, fee about $57. The link to the regulator in the card is unconfirmed. Other trackers for 2026 give a significantly different threshold: around €815 per month, closer to €9,800 per year, or a one-time amount of 408,000 leks based on a 2023 reference without a recent amendment found. A two-fold difference. For the post, this is more important than just the number. Albania is only inexpensive in one database.

The discrepancies are less pronounced in other cases. Ecuador, Visa Nómada based on rentista: around $17,352 per year, which amounts to $1,446 per month, three local minimum wages at $482 each. Duration is 24 months, registry fee about $300, while on other summaries it is $400-450. The country uses the dollar, the threshold is not affected by the exchange rate. There is a path to permanent residency after 21 months, but it is no longer a nomad visa, rather a separate residency requirement.

Brazil, VITEM XIV: from $18,000 per year or $1,500 per month, or this amount in the account. The duration is 12 months with an extension up to 24, processing takes about 15 days, fee around $136. Here, the registry has a link to an official source, and neighboring summaries confirm the figure. The condition is stricter for the money: remote work for a foreign company, not a local contract.

For comparison, consider a typical European route. In 2026, Spain requires 200% of the minimum wage. SMI - €1,221 per month. This equates to about €2,849 per month, or €34,188 per year per person. The first family member adds 75% of SMI, each subsequent member adds 25%. Greece asks for €3,500 net, not gross. UAE for virtual work - about $3,500 per month. The Thai DTV is not based on a salary but on the remaining amount from 500,000 baht.

A significant shift this year is not in the threshold but in the closed door. As of June 30, 2026, Canada is not accepting new applications for the Start-Up Visa. This is a different category, founder-based, but it fell off the map just when nomad lists started to look stable.

The practical conclusion from the registry is brief. A low figure in the aggregator is a reason to review the law, not to buy a ticket. Albania exemplifies this better than anyone: one database gives $4,845 per year, the other provides almost twice as much, and neither can replace a consular certificate on the day of application.

Magic Eden users who listed NFTs on Ethereum should revoke their approvals. On September 25, CirrusNFT spotted one wallet taking 3,832 NFTs from hundreds of wallets through Magic Eden sales at 0 ETH.

Yuga Labs CEO Michael Figge said the vulnerability was found hours earlier. 0xQuit is securing the assets in a white-hat operation. NFTs at 0x71cF...fe33 are reportedly safe and will be returned once the risk is removed.

The suspected cause is old approvals for a contract of the former Ethereum marketplace, closed in spring 2026. The haul was estimated at $1.4 million, but that figure is unconfirmed.

📌 How will ESMA supervise crypto firms under MiCA in 2027? 

📣 The European Securities and Markets Authority has set operational resilience, outsourcing and sufficient EU based operations among its main crypto supervisory priorities for 2027 as the bloc moves further into enforcement of the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation. 

🌐 ESMA said in its 2027 work program published Monday that its work on MiCA will concentrate on coordinating national regulators and developing more consistent supervision of crypto asset service providers across the European Union. The program comes as the regulator moves from writing and implementing MiCA rules toward overseeing how licensed firms comply with them in practice.  Chair Verena Ross described the change during a meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, saying ESMA’s MiCA work had moved “from rulemaking towards supervision and convergence.” 

⭐️ Operational resilience will be one of the main areas under scrutiny as ESMA works with national competent authorities responsible for supervising CASPs. Outsourcing risks, liquidity, reverse solicitation and the classification of crypto assets are among the other areas identified for coordinated work in 2027. Supervisors will pay attention to whether firms maintain sufficient operations within the EU instead of relying heavily on functions or infrastructure based elsewhere.

The Arbitrage Engine Is Already Running

Let's talk about that brand-new pool you just saw launch. How does it earn anything on day one? The answer is simple: Arbitrage.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

This isn't theoretical volume. Even today, with only a handful of live pools on Gala Swap, millions of dollars in arbitrage volume are flowing through the platform daily. Every single one of those trades pays a fee to the liquidity provider (LP).

Real Volume, Real Fees (Not "Farm Token" Emissions)

This is what makes Gala Swap different. The yield isn't based on inflationary "farm token" emissions that you have to constantly race against.

The LP rewards on Gala Swap are generated by real trading activity—the essential work of keeping the DEX price in sync with the broader market. When you provide liquidity, you become the infrastructure that makes this flow possible, and you earn your share of the fees from that volume.

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

The current volume is impressive, but here’s what’s truly exciting: the bottleneck isn't the demand from traders; it's the surface area available for the arbitrage engine to work across.

A few dozen pools can only capture a few dozen tokens' worth of flow. Imagine this same efficient arbitrage engine running across hundreds of pools that simply don't exist yet.

The Takeaway:

The traders are ready. The volume is real. The arbitrage engine is already running. What's missing is the liquidity to serve that volume and capture those fees across a much broader range of pairs.

Gala Swap provides the infrastructure; you provide the liquidity to unlock the full potential. 🟡

The Medicare Midterm ATM

Trump has opened a pre-election cash window. His administration will send one-time $90 payments to more than 20 million Medicare Part B enrollees, framed as “nearly $100” checks to help with premiums. 

Most recipients will get direct deposits in early October; people whose premiums are paid by Medicaid, or who pay Medicare’s higher income-based surcharge, are excluded. 

The money comes from the $2 billion Medicare Improvement Fund, a reserve Congress created in 2008 for improvements to traditional Medicare. 

Trump called it a pointless Democratic “slush fund” for “waste, fraud, and abuse,” then discovered it had enough cash for an October rebate. The standard 2026 Part B premium is $202.90 a month. The $90 payment covers less than half of one month. 

Then came the larger offer. Trump again promised a $5,000 “Trump Dividend” to every adult U.S. citizen if Republicans keep Congress in November. He says tariffs and “tremendous economic success” will pay for it. 

Congress would need to authorize such payments, and even House Speaker Mike Johnson has not committed to the plan. The White House is campaigning with a conditional refund: vote Republican, unlock the prize. 

At a rally in Mobile, Alabama, Trump also addressed “Gays for Palestine”: “Let’s send them over some day to negotiate. Let’s see, you’ll never see them again.” 

The crowd got a foreign-policy joke. Retirees got $90. Americans got the country’s governing program translated into sweepstakes language. 

A Medicare fund becomes a campaign envelope. Tariffs become a jackpot. Palestine becomes a rally punchline. The midterms are still weeks away, but the cashier has already opened.

📣 Japan arrests two suspect over 81M yen crypto police scam 

🔖 Japanese police have arrested two people suspected of helping a fake police fraud group steal cryptocurrency worth approximately 81 million yen from a woman in her 40s. The victim was allegedly told that her bank card had been connected to a large money laundering investigation. According to police information cited by FNN, the group claimed a fraud case had caused 600 billion yen in losses and that around 400 accounts had been used to launder funds.

⚠️ FNN reported that the caller told the woman her card appeared among accounts connected with the supposed money laundering investigation. The caller then claimed she was close to being arrested and needed to “prove her innocence.” Police allege that the false accusation eventually led the victim to transfer cryptocurrency worth around 81 million yen. The assets were valued at approximately $515,000 using the conversion cited in reports on the case.

‼️ Investigators have not publicly identified the cryptocurrencies involved or disclosed the wallet addresses that received the assets. Available reporting therefore does not establish how the cryptocurrency was subsequently moved, converted or withdrawn. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department believes Okayama and Minamisawa participated in a larger organization. Known losses from fraud cases involving the two suspects have reached approximately 240 million yen, according to FNN.
